defectsClosed.was: bundleSchema listed required/optional fields but _schema_check only tested for MISSING keys. Unknown keys were silently accepted, so RequestId could enter a persisted semantic record with no mechanical objection. Absence from a field list was being read as closure.
defectsClosed.now: EvidenceBundle declares closed=true, additionalProperties=false and unknownFieldOutcome=EVIDENCE_BUNDLE_UNKNOWN_FIELD. requestId sits in an explicit forbiddenFields list alongside executionId, attemptId, sealedAt, timestamp, processId, cacheState and lifetimeState. The checker rejects any key outside the exact required-plus-optional union BEFORE semantic evaluation.
defectsClosed.fixture: evidence-bundle-reject-request-id (required by the patch, present and rejecting)
mutations: admit requestId into the semantic record

defectsClosed.was: Only EvidenceBundle, requiredUniverse, EvaluationEvidence, verdictDerivation and storageAdmission had field lists, none enforced as closed. Nested records had no type discipline, and a malformed node could raise rather than report.
defectsClosed.now: 14 closed record schemas: EvidenceBundle, RequiredUniverse, EvaluationEvidence, VerdictDerivation, StorageAdmission, CapabilityClosure, RetentionUnit, ContentRef, ReplayClosure, and five per-claim-shape proof records (ProofLocalMatch, ProofRelationshipMatch, ProofAggregateMatch, ProofNoMatch, ProofReason). Each carries type, exact required/optional, unknown-field outcome and enum constraints. validate() is total: nulls, scalars, arrays and malformed nested records all produce deterministic findings.

defectsClosed.was: check-evidence.py accepted factPartitionPinned=true with no reference ('transitional: pin flag without ref'), and regenerationClosureRetained=true as a legacy boolean. R3-PROBE-03 reproduced this.
defectsClosed.now: Neither field exists in any schema. Their presence is a forbidden-field violation inside the closed proof record. Every partition, predicate-semantics, policy, waiver, baseline, relation-semantics and regeneration object must be a ContentRef {kind, id} with a full-length sha256 id that resolves in the retained object store. check() additionally fails the contract itself if any schema re-admits either shortcut name.
fixtures: boolean regenerationClosureRetained replaces the typed closure

defectsClosed.was: verdictDerivation required outcomeSetDigest but nothing recomputed it. R3-PROBE-02 replaced it with an arbitrary digest and the checker returned no finding.
defectsClosed.now: outcomeSetCommitment is RECOMPUTED under the canonical grammar consumed from evaluation-proof.v1 over the complete set of (evaluationId, predicateId, outcome) triples of every activated evaluation. Omission, duplication, substitution, truncation and arbitrary digests all fail. Coverage, baseline, waivers and policy are resolvable ContentRefs; an absent baseline must be explicitly declared. Sorting and deduplication come from the grammar, so a reordering cannot change the value.
fixtures: an activated evaluation omitted from the committed set
universe commitment that does not recompute
indeterminate absorbed into an authoritative pass

defectsClosed.was: proofByOutcome.match required only a 'witness' defined as subject identity plus span anchor. A relationship finding was satisfied by a span. R3-PROBE-01 reproduced this.
defectsClosed.now: Obligations are consumed per claim shape from evaluation-proof.v1. relationship-match requires relationSemanticsRef plus witnessEdges each carrying fromSubjectId, toSubjectId, relationKind and a resolvable factRef; spanAnchor is a FORBIDDEN field on that record so a relation cannot be dressed up as a located claim. no-match binds the subject-set commitment recomputed from the retained fact partition, subjectCount, completeness=complete, factPartitionRef and predicateSemanticsRef.
fixtures: relationship claim proved by a source span alone
absence claim from a sampled witness

defectsClosed.was: evidence.v1 had a pinnedEvidenceUnits string list checked only for membership. No mapping from proof references to retention units existed.
defectsClosed.now: The bundle carries a capabilityClosure whose commitment recomputes, and every proof reference required for the sealed capability must map to exactly one retention unit — omission and aliasing both reject. E12 enforces that a unit is available only if every object it holds is available, so a partially available unit confers no authority. The lattice ranks are cross-read from retention-tiers.v6 and the checker fails if they disagree. Evidence v2 defines no lease, purge, demotion or D9 semantics of its own.
fixtures: a required proof reference maps to no retention unit
a partially available unit still confers verifiable authority
mutations: let a partially available unit keep authority

defectsClosed.was: producerDeclaredObligation was checked as a semantic value (E3) but was not structurally excluded, so a producer field could still be persisted.
defectsClosed.now: producerDeclaredObligation and producerAssertedAdequacy are forbidden fields on EvaluationEvidence — structurally unrepresentable, and additionally reported as E3. Attempt metadata (RequestId, ExecutionId, attempt identity, timestamps, process identity, cache/lifetime state) is forbidden on EvidenceBundle. authorityAndLayering records what a provider may and may not do.
fixtures: producer self-declares a weaker proof obligation
mutations: let a producer declare its own obligation
